canonical_claim: GC journal-only mutations do not route through the facade and do not invalidate retained views because they do not change committed refs or committed `RootRef::mutable_files`.

Normal rounds and healthy `REBUILD` apply every returned runtime retirement before downstream work and proceed only for `{Authoritative, DrainComplete}`; damaged-state `REBUILD` uses a no-parent, zero-catalog-mutation path.

`NETWORK_ERROR` was chosen for CAS retry-later failures because it is outside the merge exemption set, participates in ClickHouse's transient retry taxonomy, and does not receive conflicting special handling on the CAS commit path.

`getResultObjectETag()` exposes the PUT or multipart-completion ETag after the upload finalize barrier so CA can record an incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD.; `WriteBufferFromFileBase` exposes `getResultObjectETag`, and `WriteBufferFromFileDecorator` forwards it so a CAS writer can record the written incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD request. Additionally, The ETag fix makes `WriteBufferFromS3` return the `PutObject` or `CompleteMultipartUpload` response ETag, eliminating the head-after-put `HEAD`.

The writer-side `RetireView`, its syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed; `MountLease` loses `observed_gc_round`, the beat publishes only `{now, min_active}`, and GC round recovery no longer uses `min_ack` or `max_ack`.; The build watermark min_active is carried in the mount lease; the standalone watermark object and writer-side observed_gc_round retired-view machinery were removed. Liveness and the `min_active` build-watermark floor are carried in one `MountLeaseKeeper` slot.; Each server maintains one merged heartbeat object at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, replacing the separate `roots/<server-hex>/_watermark` object and `WatermarkKeeper`.
Logs for one table must be folded in strict ID order, and a clamp must stop that table at the correct log; prefetching may change only when data is available, never what is applied.

The two-level write API puts terminal committed-ref primitives and `republishRef` in the facade, while `publishEntries` replaces the near-duplicate publish body of `adoptPartFromManifest` and transaction staging remains in the transaction.
`applyRefLogTxn` applies a complete transaction atomically or throws, never mutating state on throw; the same validator is used by writer, recovery, fsck, and snapshot construction.

`deleteExact` propagates transient, throttle, and authentication errors instead of forgetting the entry, while `TokenMismatch` and `NotFound` remain terminal outcomes for the exact-token deletion attempt.

The ref-chain complete-cut design's generation-change safety was confirmed to have no durable double-apply path: if the old PUT wins, the successor adopts it; if the successor's seal wins, the old PUT is rejected; if the generation changes before the old write is even sent, the old send is refused outright.; A valid successor seal must remain the conclusive rejection when an old I/O result returns after a generation bump, and the superseded runtime must not acknowledge, install, or publish it

An immutable catalog cut is the decoded bytes and object token from one successful `GET cas/ref_catalog`, plus a reverse index built once from those bytes; a consumer must not patch or mix that index with a later catalog GET.; A complete catalog GET is treated as an atomic object-version cut, whereas a paginated LIST stitches separately fetched pages and is not an atomic universe observation; downstream protocol can close staleness after a cut, but cannot recover a namespace omitted from the universe listing. The catalog remains the authoritative namespace universe because a single token-CAS `GET` supplies one complete object-version cut, whereas stitched paginated `LIST` results need not represent any namespace set at one instant.

Pre-CAS generation or retention pruning based only on the proposed seal can delete a run or data still referenced by a winning concurrent leader's parent seal or by the currently adopted GC snapshot, permanently wedging GC with `CORRUPTED_DATA` in `PriorEdgeCursor`; task T3 fixed it by using the parent-union-proposed generation set in commit `883c8f92d66`.; Pre-CAS generation pruning must protect the union of generations referenced by both the proposed seal and the parent seal; only generations referenced by neither may be deleted before the CAS. Additionally, Pre-CAS generation pruning must include every generation referenced by the parent seal as well as the proposed seal, because a losing leader must not delete a run referenced by the winning leader.
Read-only consumers such as fsck and inspect use the shared `replay` implementation with restart-on-vanish; fsck compares cache replay bytes with published snapshot bytes.

Task A7 serializes the manual `SYSTEM ... GC` round against the background GC loop using a dedicated gc_round_mutex rather than the scheduler's existing `mutex`, because loop() deliberately releases `mutex` before running a round so that stop() and heartbeatLoop() are not blocked; holding `mutex` across a long fold would freeze the GC heartbeat and stall shutdown.
A source-backed condemned or absent blob is re-uploaded and rechecked in a bounded loop; a tokened dependency without a retained source remains an ABORTED fail-closed backstop.
Ambiguous or conflicting catalog CAS results are reread and resolved, and a row that may still be the same exact row aborts successor work.

`RefPlan::changedRows` and `shouldDeferRound` can defer an entire fold round based on a listed tail observation, but the defer path performs no destructive work, advances no coverage cursor, and is bounded by `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`. The DEFER decision is true exactly when changed-shard count is below `fold_threshold`, no destructive decision is due, and `rounds_since_last_fold` is below `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`; otherwise the round FOLDs. The GC round DEFER mechanism bounds consecutive deferrals with `MaxDefer`; once the bound is reached, `GBegin` and weak fairness drive `GFold` so `unfolded` eventually returns to `{}`. FOLD and DEFER are mutually exclusive in an idle round: `DeferRound` is enabled only when `~GraduationDue` and its deferral condition hold, while `GBegin` is enabled for graduation or an exhausted honest defer budget.
GC deletes blob bodies with DELETE If-Match against the condemn-time body token; resurrecting with a fresh in-body tag changes the etag so the old exact-token delete misses.

Copy-forward verification requires a valid envelope, matching object kind, and recomputed logical hash equal to the key hash; any mismatch or 404 is fail-closed, with corruption reported as `CORRUPTED_DATA` and a lost-race 404 as `ABORTED`.

Fresh upload writes the body before a clean meta; dedup adoption point-reads the meta and adopts clean or absent metadata, while condemned metadata triggers resurrection. The writer point-reads metadata for condemned status, writes clean metadata after fresh body upload or resurrection, and may best-effort create clean metadata when adopting a present body with absent metadata.; Upload by placement: new content is written PUT If-None-Match:* (idempotent, dedup hit skips upload); cold reuse of an existing blob point-reads the object's per-hash .meta freshness state (Core/CasBlobMeta.h, MetaState{Clean,Condemned}) — condemned triggers resurrect with a fresh incarnation_tag, else the blob is reused as-is; this point-read replaced the old writer-side retire view.
A retained view may delay detection of `INV-NO-DANGLE` after a live manifest body is physically deleted, so fsck and corruption probes must bypass retained views or use strict validation.

A DR replica option is a `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica in another region with its own pool; fetch-by-relink applies only within one pool (`pool_uuid` equality), so a foreign-pool replica performs honest byte fetches, giving RPO ~ replication lag and RTO ~0, and covering T1/T4 but not T2 (it replicates `DROP TABLE` too).
Per-disk CAS settings such as `scratch_path`, `gc_enabled`, and `server_root_id` remain unprefixed because they are scoped by their disk block.
A forced GC fixpoint drive issues rounds on both replicas until fsck unreachable count settles; for a non-abandoning scenario the expected final `unreachable` count is zero.

The GC safety assertion is `{preview deletes} ⊆ {ca-fsck unreachable}`.; Every positive scenario requires replica-oracle SQL agreement, `clickhouse-disks cas-fsck --detail` with `dangling = 0`, and `clickhouse-disks cas-gc-dryrun` candidates contained in the quiescent `cas-fsck` unreachable set.

[C1] requires `loop()` and `heartbeatLoop()` to check `isVanished()` at each wake and self-exit, preventing new GC rounds after `Vanished`. The GC scheduler exits at its next wake on `Vanished`, on published `vanished_intent`, and on `IdentityLost`; it does not join from a callback.
A point-in-time `HEAD -> 404` is not durable absence; unreadable bodies clamp the fold and any clamped pass suppresses destructive decisions.

A non-corruption exception from `classifyRefLogOccupant` leaves the lane `Wedged` with the exact attempt retained; because equal bytes are returned as `Ours` before the throwing decode, such an exception implies foreign bytes at a write-once key and cannot lose a durable own transaction.

RustFS failed the LIST-consistency passport by omitting keys that had been durable for 19 seconds, so conservative probe-always behavior remains the default. Additionally, The fail-close default for LIST trust is probe-always, and RustFS currently fails the proposed passport by measurement. Additionally, A RustFS ref-log enumeration omitted durable predecessor keys `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` while returning later `0x1430e`; exact-key `GET` and `HEAD` still reported the omitted objects present.; The fix must tolerate an object store that returns inconsistent `LIST` results; RustFS demonstrated inconsistency and AWS S3 was untested at the time of the debt record.
All answers returned by `PartFolderView` are pure functions of that view.
A NeverBorn recovery seal needs a specified zero sealed_from exception and seal-aware fsck handling; otherwise a healthy pool whose newest snapshot is synthetic remains unchecked

On plain S3, mutation finalization can make `loadProjections` see only committed metadata, silently skip a carried-forward projection, and leave the in-memory mutated part without that projection until reload. `createHardLink` must stage the hardlink eagerly so `loadProjections` during the same finalization can see a carried-forward projection.

Epochs are crossed only by consuming a seal at the expected id; an `EpochSeal` is counted as applied with `produced=false`, and a later-epoch record reachable before its seal is held rather than guessed across.

Compression is a deterministic per-type policy of `Never`, `Always`, or `PinnedRaw` with no size threshold; `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes` are always compressed under a `.zst` key suffix, while `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` remain raw. The deterministic formats `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` are `PinnedRaw` and `Strict`, while the Always-compressed set is exactly `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes`, whose `storedSuffix` is `.zst`.

B140-dangle was caused by separately durable snapshot edges and `folded_cursor`; embedding the cursor in the snap codec makes trim and snap coverage co-durable. Additionally, `CaB140DangleMerge.tla` proves that trim gating and storing the fold cursor with committed snap edges are jointly necessary and sufficient to prevent trim-before-durable dangles.; Snapshot coverage and GC fold coverage are independent: snapshot `X` lets a writer omit logs through `X`, while the folded cursor proves that those logs no longer need to be read for edge discovery; both are required before log deletion.
The A1 benchmark's `BM_ScratchCopy` remained O(1) at about 58 ns after the restructure, and `BM_ApplyRefLogTxn` remained within measurement noise at 770–831 ns versus 800–864 ns baseline.

Phase 1 uses exactly one body-only log encoding at `_log/<txn-id>`; ref names are not encoded in object keys and invalid relative paths, including empty, `.`, `..`, repeated separators, NUL bytes, and noncanonical escaping, are rejected.
B140-dangle is pinned by tests requiring a shared deduplicated blob to survive dropping only one of two live refs.

If the hidden transaction is a removal, GC can delete blobs that the recovered writer view still references, producing a dangling committed manifest; if it is an addition, GC over-protects blobs; without a covering snapshot, recovery can repeatedly fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The resurrect-reupload orphan occurs when GC tracks a retired entry by hash only; settling the old token without re-condemning a replacement token can leave the replacement present forever.

The retired-in-snapshot plan makes each per-shard source-edge run carry condemned state at the existing zero-sentinel key, adds a per-shard `CondemnedSummary` to the fold seal, and removes `RetiredSet`, `CART`, `retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`.

Normal-class ref mutation items cannot split across chunks: an item exceeding `ref_txn_max_ops` is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` before object creation, while an item that would overflow a non-empty chunk rolls the chunk and lands whole in a fresh one. Additionally, Removal-class items are exempt from the normal op cap but carve solo as `WholeShard` mutations, so they cannot be split by a chunk boundary; their size is bounded by `ref_removal_max_bytes`.
Every fold-seal PUT must verify encodeFoldSeal(...).size() <= fold_seal_cap, with the reservation estimator accounting for JSON escaping and framing.
